sources.citation: Bargy, M. 1909. Notes ethnographiques sur les Birifons. L'Anthropologie 20: 167-174. (Glottolog ref 12601, tagged grammar_sketch)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnographic note (archive.org scanned of the volume): says only that their 'langue est différente du lobi : elle rentre dans le groupe mossi-gourounsi (ou langue yani de M. Delafosse)' (p.172) and appends 'Quelques mots lobis et birifons' (p.173); no phonology, no tone or accent.

sources.citation: Tirogo, Issoufou François & Noéllie Soubeiga. 2023. Vowel length in Kasim, Samoma and Birifor. Akofena, Varia n°10, vol. 3: 437-446 (CC BY 4.0). Birifor data are the Malba parler, taken from Tirogo 2018.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress/accent. §2.3 and §3.3 on Birifor: vowel length is 'a trait of the syllable' (citing Tirogo 2018: 89), CV/CVV and CVC/CVVC oppositions, then reanalysed (following Tirogo 'to appear') as two syllables (-V# a number suffix); all Birifor forms are tone-marked (và/và:, lár/lá:r, pɩ̀r/pɩ̀:r, bɛ́̃/bɛ́̃:, bɩ̀r/bɩ̀r-ɛ̀, láá/láύ, ɟúú/púó) but the words 'stress' and 'accent' never occur; the only prosodic remarks are that length is 'a prosodic fact' at the syllable level and that long vowels can bear 'modulated' (contour) tone.
